attributes.body_ja: 「って」は引用（いんよう）を表（あらわ）す「と」のくだけた表現（ひょうげん）ですが、それだけでなく、話題（わだい）を示（しめ）す「は」のくだけた表現（ひょうげん）にもなります。この「って」は、主（おも）に会話（かいわ）の中（なか）で使（つか）われます。「は」と同（おな）じように、文（ぶん）の話題（わだい）を示（しめ）す名詞（めいし）のあとに置（お）かれます。
attributes.body: Although って can be used as a casual quotation marker in Japanese (replacing と), it is also frequently used as a casual topic marker (replacing は). This is something that occurs primarily in spoken language, and will come directly after the sentence topic, in exactly the same way as the adverbial particle は usually would.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Difference between が and って
Using 「って」 as a casual version of 「と」

attributes.body: って casually introduces or refers back to a topic, e.g. あの人って優しいよね ('That person is really kind, huh?') なんか・なんて adds a dismissive or emotional tone, often implying downplaying or surprise, e.g. 私なんかにできるかな ('Can someone like me really do it?')

first_relatable.title: って
first_relatable.meaning: As for, Speaking of, Casual は (Sentence topic marker)

attributes.body: Both can mean 'speaking of (A)', but differ in tone and usage. といえば often refers back to something just mentioned or known to both speaker and listener, e.g. 京都といえば、お寺が有名だね ('Speaking of Kyoto, its temples are famous.') って is a casual form used in everyday conversation, often functioning like は to casually introduce a topic, e.g. この映画って最高！ ('That movie is amazing!')

first_relatable.title: といえば
first_relatable.meaning: Speaking of, If it were the case that

second_relatable.title: って
second_relatable.meaning: As for, Speaking of, Casual は (Sentence topic marker)

attributes.body: って is used in casual conversation to introduce a topic informally. It comes from the quotation particle と and can carry the nuance of 'speaking of…'. は is a more standard and flexible topic marker, used in both casual and formal situations, including writing. Unlike って, は can also carry a contrastive nuance.
